rules.title: Definition: Customs Value
rules.text: “Customs Value” means the value as determined in accordance with the WTO Agreement on implementation of Article VII of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade 1994 (WTO Agreement on customs valuation);
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Defines the Customs Value field stored for every input.

rules.title: Definition: Ex-works Price
rules.text: “Ex-works Price” means the price paid for the Product ex-works to the manufacturer in the States Party in whose undertaking the last working or processing is carried out, provided the price includes the value of all the Materials used minus any internal taxes paid which are, or may be, repaid when the Product obtained is exported;
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Denominator of the tolerance share. Missing ex-works price -> 'Further information required (missing)' when the share is needed.

rules.title: Definition: Material
rules.text: “Material” means any ingredient, raw material, component or part used in the Manufacture of a Product;
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Every bill-of-materials line is treated as a Material.

rules.title: Definition: Value Added
rules.text: "Value Added" means the difference between the ex-works price of a finished Product and the Customs Value of the Material imported from outside the State Parties and used in the production; [footnote 2: This definition is an outstanding provision]
rules.legal_status: Outstanding provision (footnoted in the Agreement text; see Annex 2 Art. 42)
rules.engine_behaviour: Not used in the calculation (19.01 rule has no value-added test). Shown for reference only.

rules.title: Definition: Value of Materials
rules.text: “Value of Materials” means the Customs Value at the time of importation of the non-originating Materials used, or if this is not known and cannot be ascertained, the first ascertainable price paid for the Materials in any State Party.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Default valuation basis for the 15% tolerance (group decision Q1): Customs Value; if not known, the stated first ascertainable price in a State Party, labelled as fallback.

rules.title: Origin conferring criteria
rules.text: A Product shall be considered as originating from a State Party if it has: (a) been wholly obtained in that State Party within the meaning of Article 5 of this Annex; or (b) undergone substantial transformation in that State Party within the meaning of Article 6 of this Annex.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Frames the assessment: 19.01 products are assessed under Art. 4(b) via Art. 6(2).

rules.title: Wholly obtained products (chapeau and (b), (m))
rules.text: 1. The following Products shall be considered as wholly obtained in a State Party when exported to another State Party: … (b) plants, including aquatic plants and plant Products, vegetables and fruits, grown or harvested therein; … (m) Goods produced therein exclusively from the Products specified in subparagraphs (a) to (l); …
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')

rules.title: Sufficiently worked or processed Products – criteria
rules.text: 1. For purposes of Article 4(b) of this Annex, Products which are not wholly obtained are considered to be sufficiently worked or processed when they fulfil one of the following criteria: (a) Value Added; (b) non-originating Material content; (c) change in tariff Heading; or (d) specific processes.

rules.title: Cumulation of origin within the AfCFTA
rules.text: 1. For purposes of implementing this Article, all State Parties shall be considered as a single Territory. 2. Raw Materials or semi-finished Goods originating in any of the State Parties and undergoing working or processing in another State Party, shall be deemed to have originated in the State Party where the final processing or manufacturing takes place. 3. Working or processing carried out in any of the State Parties shall be considered as having been carried out in the State Parties when the Materials undergo further working or processing in a State Party. 4. Notwithstanding paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, Products further manufactured in a State Party shall be considered as originating in a State Party where the last manufacturing process takes place provided that the last working or processing operations exceed those operations under Article 7 of this Annex.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: A 19.01 input originating in another State Party counts as originating only with proof under Art. 31(1). Box 12 code SC is suggested when this is relied on.

rules.title: Unit of qualification
rules.text: 1. The unit of qualification for the application of the provisions of this Annex shall be the particular Product, which is considered as a basic unit when determining classification. 2. For purposes of this Annex: (a) the tariff classification of a particular Product or Material shall be determined according to the Harmonized System; (b) a Product composed of a group or assembly of articles or components is classified pursuant to the terms of the HS under a single Heading or Sub-heading, the whole shall constitute a unit of qualification; and (c) where a shipment consists of a number of identical Products classified under the same Heading or Sub-heading of the Harmonised System, each Product shall be considered separately.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: One product per case; HS codes are taken as declared and checked for plausibility only.

rules.title: Treatment of packing (separate determination)
rules.text: 1. Where for purposes of assessing customs duties, a State Party treats Goods separately from their packing, it may also, in respect of its imports consigned from another State Party, determine separately the origin of such packing.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Limitation note: the importing State Party may determine packing origin separately; the tool cannot know this.

rules.title: Treatment of packing (transport/storage packing)
rules.text: 2. Where paragraph 1 of this Article is not applicable, packing shall be considered as forming a whole with the Goods and no part of any packing required for their transportation or storage shall be considered as having been imported from outside the State Party when determining the origin of the Goods as a whole.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')
rules.engine_behaviour: Transport/storage packing is not treated as imported; no finding.

rules.title: Treatment of packing (retail packing)
rules.text: 3. For purposes of paragraph 2 of this Article, packing with which Goods are ordinarily sold at retail shall not be regarded as packing required for the transportation or storage of Goods.

rules.title: Transitional arrangements – outstanding issues
rules.text: 1. State Parties agree that the following issues are outstanding: (a) Implementing decisions on the definitions of “Value Added” in Article 1 (x) and requirements for “their vessels” and “their factory ships” in Article 5(2) and criteria and issues pertaining to Special Economic Arrangements/Zones In Article 9 in Annex 2 on Rules of Origin; (b) Drafting of additional definitions in Annex 2 on Rules of Origin; (c) Drafting hybrid rules in Appendix IV to Annex 2 on the Rules of Origin; (d) Drafting Regulations for Goods produced under Special Economic Arrangements/Zones; (e) Drafting of additional provisions in Annex 2 on Rules of Origin on value tolerance, absorption principle and accounting segregation/GAAP; and (f) Drafting AfCFTA Rules of Origin Manuals/Guidelines. 2. The outstanding provisions referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall, upon adoption by the Assembly, form an integral part of this Annex. 3. Pending the adoption of the outstanding provisions, State Parties agree that the Rules of Origin in existing trade regimes shall be applicable.
rules.legal_status: Agreement text as published by Laws.Africa ('as at 21 March 2018')

rules.title: Introductory Note 1.1
rules.text: 1.1 The rules set out in Column 3 of this Appendix are the minimum conditions required for the concerned Products to be considered as sufficiently worked or processed within the meaning of paragraph 2 of Article 6 of Annex 2 on Rules of Origin.
rules.legal_status: Approved by the 12th AfCFTA Council of Ministers, December 2023

rules.title: Introductory Note 2.1
rules.text: 2.1: The first two columns in the Appendix describe the Product obtained. The first column gives the Chapter, Heading or Sub-heading as it is used in the Harmonized System (HS). The second column gives the description of Goods as it is used in the HS for that Chapter, Heading or Sub-heading. For each entry in the first two columns a rule is specified in Column 3. Where, in some cases, the entry in the first column is preceded by an “ex”, this signifies that the rules in Column 3 apply only to the part of that Chapter, Heading or Sub-as described in Column 2.
rules.legal_status: Approved by the 12th AfCFTA Council of Ministers, December 2023
rules.engine_behaviour: Basis for using Column 2 descriptions as HS descriptions for input classification (group decision Q7).

rules.title: Introductory Note 2.4
rules.text: 2.4: Where a Chapter, Heading or Sub-heading, in Column 1, or any text of this Appendix, is in square brackets that is an indication that the rule for that Chapter, Heading or Sub-heading in Column 3, or that text, is yet to be agreed by the AfCFTA Negotiating Institutions.

rules.title: Absorption Principle (draft)
rules.text: The value of the non-originating Materials used by the Producer in the production of a Product shall not include, for purposes of calculating the value of the product, the value of non-originating Materials used to produce originating Materials that are subsequently used in the production of the Product.

rules.title: Accounting Segregation (draft)
rules.text: Where originating and non-originating fungible Materials are used in the production of Products, the following methods shall be adopted in determining whether the Materials used are originating: a) physical separation of the Materials; or b) an inventory management method recognized in the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles of the exporting State Party, provided that the inventory management method selected is used for at least one (1) fiscal year.”

rules.title: Tolerance Rule (draft) – APPLIED
rules.text: 1. Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 6, non-originating Materials which, according to the conditions set out in Appendix IV to this Annex shall not be used in the Manufacture of a given Product, may, nevertheless be used, provided that: b) Their total value does not exceed 15 per cent of the Ex-works Price of the final Product; c) The percentage given in paragraphs (a) of this paragraph shall not exceed any of the percentages for the maximum content of non-originating Materials as outlined in the Product Specific Rules laid out in Appendix IV. 1. Paragraph 1 of this Article shall not apply to Products falling within Chapters 50 through 63. 2. The tolerance in this Article shall be applied subject to the provisions of Article 7.
rules.provision: EX.CL/Draft/Dec…(XL) Annex, item 3 (lettering as printed: b), c) with no a))
rules.legal_status: Draft decision text, adoption not confirmed in attached sources
rules.engine_behaviour: APPLIED, always on (group decision). Sum ALL non-originating 19.01 materials; share = sum / ex-works price compared exactly (sum*100 <= 15*price). Paragraph (c) has no effect for 19.01 (no maximum percentage in the row). Article 7 is checked in every case.
rules.notes: Value tolerance is also listed as outstanding in Annex 2 Art. 42(1)(e).

rules.title: Additional introductory note on CTSH (draft)
rules.text: Pursuant to paragraph 2 of Article 6 of the Annex, in this Appendix the Change of Tariff Sub-Heading (CTSH) shall apply as follows: i. The non-originating materials used must be classified under a sub-heading other than that of the final product. ii. Sub-headings may appear in the same heading or in different headings.
rules.legal_status: Draft decision text, adoption not confirmed in attached sources
rules.engine_behaviour: Reference only: the 19.01 rule is a heading change, not CTSH.

rules.title: Definition of Value Added (draft)
rules.text: Value Added means the difference between the ex-works price of a finished Product and the Customs Value of the Material imported from outside the State Parties and used in the Production.
rules.legal_status: Draft decision text, adoption not confirmed in attached sources
rules.engine_behaviour: Reference only.

rules.title: FOB as basis of calculation of VNOM (draft)
rules.text: FOB shall be the basis of the calculation of the Value of Non-originating materials (VNOM).
rules.legal_status: Draft decision text, adoption not confirmed in attached sources
rules.engine_behaviour: Alternative valuation basis. Computed alongside Customs Value; shown when it changes the outcome (group decision Q1).

rules.title: State Party list (draft decision, Jan 2022)
rules.text: REITERATES its congratulations to the thirty nine (39) State Parties who deposited their instruments of ratification of the AfCFTA Agreement with the Chairperson of the Commission, namely: Angola, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Côte d’Ivoire, Congo, Djibouti, Egypt, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Lesotho, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Saharawi Arab Democratic Republic, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda and Zimbabwe;
rules.legal_status: Draft decision text, adoption not confirmed in attached sources
rules.engine_behaviour: Only the 34 named countries are used as State Party suppliers (group decision Q2). Dated January 2022; may be outdated.
rules.notes: Text says 39 but names 34; para. 6 adds Burundi and Seychelles; report para. 3 says 40. Not resolved in attached sources.

rules.title: Provisional application of REC rules (draft decision)
rules.text: ENDORSES the Guidelines for the Provisional Application of Rules of Origin for the remaining outstanding tariff lines in accordance with existing trade regimes or Regional Economic Communities, pending the adoption of all outstanding issues in the Rules of Origin negotiations, in line with Article 42(3) of Annex 2 of the Protocol on Trade in Goods

decisions.decision: The 15% tolerance (EXCL-AN-3) is applied, always on, although it is draft decision text.
The Ex-Chapter 19 wheat condition is not applied because the 19.01 row governs; shown as an information note.
Valuation basis for the tolerance: Customs Value (Art. 1(y)); FOB (EXCL-AN-7) computed alongside and shown when it changes the outcome.
State Party suppliers are drawn only from the 34 countries named in EX.CL draft decision para. 7; non-State-Party suppliers are non-African countries.
Severity: critical = rule text says the certificate would fail; major = cannot be assessed without new evidence; minor = resolvable form or consistency issue.
A determinate critical failure overrides missing data; missing items are still listed.
Operation map (Art. 7(1) letters vs. not-listed vs. unclear) is a group interpretation of Art. 7(1) and 7(3).
Input HS codes use Appendix IV Column 1–2 descriptions (Note 2.1) at heading level where a row exists, otherwise chapter level.
Any food-aid input makes the product fail (Art. 7(2) 'partially obtained').
All values in GHS; mixed currency on a relevant input = contradictory (no exchange-rate source).
Box 12 suggestion: SX; SC when a State-Party 19.01 input is counted as originating. Always indicative.
Repeated error = same error type on same field logged twice or more -> bug report to model development team.
